grade.first_issue: After deriving a sine-law constraint, the submission simply asserts that the angle conditions force ((\vec o-\vec{O'})\cdot\vec{BC}=0). No argument connects that constraint to the circumcentre equations. This is the decisive unsupported central inference covered by Rule E.
grade.summary: The proof correctly reformulates OM=ON as the statement that O lies on the perpendicular bisector of MN, and it derives some valid sine-law relations. However, the central geometric/algebraic implication is replaced by an unsupported appeal to “symmetry”; no such symmetry has been established, and the configuration is generally not symmetric. Proving this implication requires essentially the missing core of the problem, not a bounded local repair.
strengths: Correctly computes the powers of M and N and reduces OM=ON to \(\vec o\cdot(\vec c-\vec b)=(|\vec c|^2-|\vec b|^2)/4\).
Correctly identifies \(O'=(\vec b+\vec c)/4\) as the midpoint of MN and reduces the goal to \(OO'\perp BC\).
The displayed sine-law relations are broadly consistent with the stated angle equalities and midpoint lengths.

errors.description: The claim that the angle conditions and the displayed sine relation ensure \(OO'\perp BC\) is entirely unproved. It is essentially a restatement of the desired conclusion and supplies no use of the equations characterizing the circumcentre of \(AKL\).
The asserted “symmetry of the angle conditions across the midline” has not been established and is not an evident symmetry of a general scalene configuration; it cannot justify the projection claim.
The scalar symbols \(b,c\) in the sine-law formulas are not defined after \(\vec b,\vec c\) were introduced as vectors, although they can be inferred as the customary side lengths.
